products.title: Azolla (Fairy Moss)
products.body_html:
Want surface cover that works as a nutrient sponge? Azolla is a floating fern with tiny overlapping leaves that form a soft mat across the water. It shades out algae, strips nitrate fast, and turns red or bronze under strong light or cool weather.

What You’ll Receive

Our Azolla is sold by portion size and packed in resealable bags. The dimensions below refer to the approximate bag size, not the coverage area after the plants are released into your aquarium or pond.

Portion Size Approx. Bag Size Suggested Count Notes
Small 2" × 2" 20+ Great starter portion for nano aquariums and small ponds.
Medium 3" × 3" 80+ Ideal for medium aquariums and water gardens.
Large 4" × 4" 320+ Best value for large aquariums, ponds, and rapid propagation.

Please Note:

  • Plant counts are approximate since Azolla plants naturally vary in size.
  • Azolla is extremely small and reproduces rapidly under suitable growing conditions, so the number of plants will increase over time.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Fairy Moss, Water Fern, Mosquito Fern
  • Scientific name — Azolla caroliniana
  • Placement — Floating
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium to high. Strong light is what turns it red
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 65–85°F · pH 5.5–7.5
  • Substrate — Not required. Feeds entirely from the water column
  • Propagation — Fragmentation

Grower’s Notes

  • Keep the surface calm. Azolla will not tolerate strong agitation or spray — water sitting on the fronds rots them. Aim filter outflow below the surface or fence the plants off from the turbulence.
  • Thin it weekly. It doubles quickly and a closed mat shades everything below, including your other plants. Scoop out a third at a time.
  • Red color comes from bright light and cool water, not fertilizer. In a dim warm tank it stays green.
  • It fixes nitrogen through a symbiotic cyanobacterium in its leaves, which is why it grows so fast in water most plants find lean.

Want to go deeper? Read our guide to the Best Floating Plants for Freshwater Aquariums.

Notes

  • Azolla grows rapidly and may require regular thinning in well-lit or nutrient-rich environments. Not recommended for tanks with strong surface agitation or high flow.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Limnophila Rugosa
products.body_html:
The Limnophila that isn't feathery. Limnophila rugosa breaks with its genus entirely — broad, textured, basil-like leaves in bright green instead of the fine whorled foliage sessiliflora and aromatica are known for. Bushy and dense, and unmistakable next to anything else in a planted tank.

What You’ll Receive

Sold as loose fresh-cut plants, bunched plants, or potted plants:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Approx. 4 loose-cut stems without root
  • Bunched Plants: Approx. 4 stems without root, bundled with foam and a plant weight
  • Potted Plants: Approx. 4 stems without root, potted in rockwool and net pot

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Limnophila Rugosa
  • Scientific name — Limnophila rugosa
  • Also known as — Basil-Leaf Limnophila, Limnophila Butterfly
  • Origin — Tropical Asia
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • Broad leaves are the whole point. If your scape already has fine-textured stems, adding another feathery plant just adds bulk. Rugosa's wide crinkled leaves give contrast within the same growth form.
  • Grown emersed it produces a distinct scent from the leaves — the plant is used as a herb in parts of its native range.
  • Trim the tops and replant them; repeated topping builds density.
  • Plant stems an inch apart. Broad leaves shade each other badly when crowded, and the lower leaves drop.
  • Feed at the roots as well as the water column — the large leaves need the input.

products.title: Dracaena Sanderiana – Lucky Bamboo
products.body_html:
🎋 Dracaena sanderiana – Lucky Bamboo
Semi-Aquatic Ornamental Plant | Can Grow in Aquariums with Emerged Foliage

Dracaena sanderiana, widely known as Lucky Bamboo, is a beautiful and resilient ornamental plant often used in aquariums, paludariums, and indoor decorative displays. Despite its common name, Lucky Bamboo is not a true bamboo but a member of the Dracaena family. Its smooth green stems and elegant narrow leaves create a clean, minimal aesthetic that pairs beautifully with modern aquascapes and indoor plant arrangements.

One unique feature of Dracaena sanderiana is that the stem can safely grow in aquarium water, making it popular for aquarists who want a plant that bridges both aquatic and terrestrial environments. The stems tolerate full submersion, but the leaves are not adapted for underwater life.

When fully submerged, the leaves will typically decline and melt after a short period of time. For long-term health, the leaves should grow above the water line, where they will continue to develop normally and can thrive permanently in that position. This makes Lucky Bamboo ideal for aquariums where the stem is placed in water while the foliage grows above the tank.

🌟 Key Features

Scientific Name: Dracaena sanderiana
Common Name: Lucky Bamboo
Plant Type: Semi-aquatic ornamental houseplant

• Aquarium Compatible Stem: The stem can grow submerged in aquarium water.
• Emergent Growth Habit: Leaves must grow above the water surface for long-term health.
• Elegant Upright Structure: Smooth green stalks with narrow pointed leaves create a clean decorative look.
• Versatile Placement: Perfect for aquariums, paludariums, ripariums, and indoor plant displays.

🌱 Growth & Care

Lighting: Low to moderate light
Water Parameters: Adaptable to most aquarium conditions
Placement: Stem can be placed underwater, but leaves must remain above water
Growth Form: Upright stem plant with emergent foliage

Important:
While the stem tolerates submersion, the leaves will only survive a short time underwater. For permanent growth in an aquarium environment, position the plant so that the foliage grows above the water line.

🪴 Aquarium & Decorative Benefits

• Natural Aquascape Accent: Adds vertical structure and a natural look to aquariums.
• Perfect for Open-Top Tanks: Ideal for aquariums where plants can grow above the water surface.
• Low Maintenance: Hardy and adaptable, making it suitable for beginners and experienced hobbyists alike.

📦 What You’ll Receive

Fresh, healthy Dracaena sanderiana (Lucky Bamboo) carefully prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®:

Fresh Cut Plant:
• 1 healthy stem cutting approximately 8–12 inches tall with attached leaves.

⚠️ Care Disclaimer

Dracaena sanderiana is commonly used in aquariums, but only the stem should remain submerged.
Leaves are not aquatic and will not survive permanently underwater.

For best long-term results, position the plant so the stem grows in water while the leaves grow above the aquarium.

Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Cardamine Lyrata
products.body_html:
A stem plant that behaves like a vine. Cardamine lyrata — Japanese Cress — carries small, round, ivy-like leaves on long trailing stems that creep across hardscape or climb toward the surface rather than standing upright. It also prefers cooler water than most tropical stems.

What You’ll Receive

  • Sold as a Small Bare-root Plants, Bunched plants, or Potted plants
  • Small bare-root | small rooted develop plants
  • Bunched plants | rooted plants bundle with foam, and plant weight
  • Potted plants | rooted developed plants potted with net pot and rock wool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Cardamine
  • Scientific name — Cardamine lyrata
  • Also known as — Japanese Cress, Chinese Ivy
  • Origin — East Asia
  • Placement — Midground; also trails over hardscape
  • Mature height — 4–10 in
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 65–75°F · pH 6.5–7.5. Note the ceiling — this is a cool-water species
  • Substrate — Not required, though a nutrient substrate gives fuller growth
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed in humid terrariums
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem sections

Grower’s Notes

  • Keep it under 75°F. Cardamine comes from temperate East Asia and thins out badly in a warm tropical tank. It suits room-temperature, lightly heated and coldwater setups — which is where most of its competition won't grow.
  • Train it rather than plant it. Laid across wood or stone the stems creep and root as they go, giving a draped effect no upright stem plant produces.
  • It arrives in emersed nursery form with round leaves. Submerged growth comes in a slightly different shape — that's the plant adapting, not a mislabel.
  • Trim and replant cuttings; sections root readily from any node.
  • Fast growth means regular trimming, or it reaches the surface and shades what's below.

Notes

  • Cardamine lyrata ships in its emersed nursery form with round leaves. Once submerged, leaf shape may change and adapt to aquarium conditions. Some initial melting or leaf loss may occur during transition but new submerged growth will follow.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Rotala Rotundifolia
products.body_html:
The Rotala to start with. Rotala rotundifolia grows small round leaves in opposite pairs on fast, upright stems, and shifts from bright green to a pink or reddish tone under strong light. It's the most forgiving plant in a genus with a reputation for being demanding — and it grows fast enough to fill a background in weeks.

What You’ll Receive

  • Sold as an emerged loose Fresh-cut plants, Bunched plants, or Potted plants
  • Fresh-cut plants | Approx. 6 stems, loose fresh-cut stems without root
  • Bunched plants | Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems without root, bundled with foam, and lead weight
  • Potted plants | Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems without root, potted with net pot and rockwool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Rotala Rotundifolia
  • Scientific name — Rotala rotundifolia
  • Also known as — Round-leaved Rotala, Pink Sprite, Dwarf Rotala
  • Origin — Southeast Asia
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium to high. Color tracks light closely
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Nutrient substrate or root tabs recommended
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • Color is free here, not bought. Unlike the demanding red Rotala, rotundifolia pinks up on light alone — no CO₂ and no nitrate starvation required. In a low-tech tank it stays green and healthy, which is a perfectly good outcome.
  • The leaves you receive are emersed-grown and rounder. Submerged growth comes in narrower and often pinker — the plant hasn't been mislabeled, it has changed form.
  • Trim the tops and replant them. Repeated topping is what turns six stems into a dense hedge.
  • Plant stems individually an inch apart. Bunched, the lower stems shade out and drop leaves.

products.title: Bacopa Salzmannii 'Purple'
products.body_html:
Want purple that doesn't wash out? Bacopa salzmannii 'Purple' — the Singapore variant — carries magenta to deep purple on the stems and on both leaf surfaces, including the undersides and shaded growth. Unlike standard salzmannii, it holds that color above water as well as below.

  • Scientific name — Bacopa salzmannii 'Purple'
  • Origin — Cultivated form; the species is South American
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6+ fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in

products.title: Ludwigia Pantanal Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
One of the hardest reds worth growing. Ludwigia inclinata var. verticillata 'Pantanal' carries narrow needle-like leaves in whorls, coloring from pink through to fiery red — a texture and color combination almost nothing else in the hobby offers. It also demands high light, CO₂ and soft water to show it. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® format.

What You'll Receive

  • 4-inch sealed Vitro Culture® bag of Ludwigia Pantanal
  • Each bag contains multiple healthy plantlets, ready for immediate planting

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Ludwigia Pantanal
  • Scientific name — Ludwigia sp. 'Pantanal'
  • Also known as — Ludwigia inclinata var. verticillata 'Pantanal'
  • Origin — Pantanal wetlands, South America
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Mature height — 6–14 in
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. High light is what produces the red
  • CO₂ — Recommended, in practice near-essential for color
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.0. Soft, low-carbonate water with good flow
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich substrate
  • Growth habit — Amphibious, but colors and forms best submerged
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower's Notes

  • Pantanal punishes instability. It reacts to swings in CO₂, light period or fertilization faster than almost any other stem plant — usually by dropping its lower leaves. Have the tank running steadily before you add it.
  • Soft water is not optional. Pantanal wants low carbonate hardness. In hard alkaline tap water it stunts at the tips whatever else you do — test KH rather than chasing a pH number.
  • Good flow matters as much as light. Stagnant water shows up as stunted tips.
  • Trim the tops and replant them — cuttings color faster than the stumps regrow. Tissue culture removes the pest risk but not the demands, so expect a short adaptation period and green early growth.
  • If this is a step too far, Ludwigia Super Red Mini gives deep red on a far more forgiving plant.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Ludwigia Care Guide.

Notes

  • Ludwigia Pantanal requires high light, CO₂, and a nutrient-rich environment to display its red hues. Expect a short adaptation period after planting.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Cryptocoryne Pink Flamingo Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Want genuine pink rather than red? Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Pink Flamingo' is one of the few aquarium plants that delivers it — wavy, textured leaves in light pink to rose on a compact rosette. It is also one of the most demanding Crypts in the hobby, and worth understanding before you buy.

What You’ll Receive

One 4-inch sealed Vitro Culture® bag containing healthy Cryptocoryne 'Pink Flamingo' plantlets — ready to rinse, acclimate, and plant in your aquarium.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Pink Flamingo Crypt
  • Scientific name — Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Pink Flamingo'
  • Also known as — Crypt Flamingo, Cryptocoryne Pink Panther
  • Origin — Cultivated form; the species is native to Sri Lanka
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Mature height — 3–5 in
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced
  • Light — Medium to high. Strong light intensifies the pink
  • CO₂ — Recommended. It holds color and compact form far better with it
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.5–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Substrate runners, slowly

Grower’s Notes

  • The pink is why it is difficult. Pink leaves carry far less chlorophyll than green ones, so this plant photosynthesizes less efficiently than any standard wendtii and has much less margin for poor light, unstable conditions or neglect. Treat it as an advanced plant regardless of how easy ordinary Crypt Wendtii is.
  • Expect a heavy melt. All Crypts shed leaves on a change of conditions, and Pink Flamingo does it harder than most. Leave it alone for three to four weeks and let it rebuild from the roots — pulling it up is what turns a recoverable melt into a loss.
  • Feed at the roots and don't move it. Crypts melt again every time they are relocated, and this one is slow enough that a second melt costs months.
  • New growth often returns greener before the pink comes back. Judge the color once it has settled, not on the first leaves.

Three ways to buy this plant. This listing is the 4-inch Vitro Culture® bag — several sterile plantlets, the best value per plant. There is also an established bare-root or potted plant if you want size now, and a small Vitro Culture® cup with one small rooted plant — the cheapest way in, and the slowest.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Cryptocoryne Care Guide.

Notes

  • Photos are sample representations. Actual coloration may vary depending on lighting, CO₂, and nutrient availability. Melting may occur during the transition to submerged growth, but healthy regrowth is expected under stable care.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Ludwigia Tornado Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Ludwigia Tornado is the stem plant that looks like it is caught mid-spin. Each narrow leaf twists into a corkscrew as it grows, so a planted group reads as motion rather than a flat wall of foliage. Color runs olive-green to rust and red depending on how hard the tank is driven.

What You'll Receive

Fresh, healthy Ludwigia Tornado Vitro Culture® cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®, available in multiple value packs:

  • 1 Bag: One 4-inch Vitro Culture® bag filled with many small plantlets
  • 5 Bags: Five 4-inch Vitro Culture® bags (excellent for larger aquascapes or propagation)
  • 10 Bags: Ten 4-inch Vitro Culture® bags (ideal for larger tank coverage)

Each 4-inch bag contains multiple young plants, which can be separated and grown into numerous individual stems—offering exceptional value and flexibility for aquascaping.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Tornado Ludwigia
  • Scientific name — Ludwigia inclinata var. verticillata 'Curly'
  • Also known as — Ludwigia Twister, Ludwigia Curly
  • Origin — Central and South America
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — 4-inch bag of small plantlets, straight-leaved on arrival
  • Mature height — 6-14 inches
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Nutrient-rich soil or root tabs, plus water column dosing
  • Growth habit — Amphibious stem, feeds from roots and water column
  • Propagation — Cuttings

Grower's Notes

  • The curl is a light response, not a fixed trait. Under medium light the leaves loosen and flatten out. Strong light directly overhead is what tightens them into the spiral this variety is sold for.
  • Expect straight leaves out of the bag. Tissue culture plantlets are grown emersed and arrive without the twist. The curled form appears on the new submersed growth over the following few weeks.
  • Iron drives the red. Without a comprehensive micronutrient dose the plant grows well but stays green. Regular iron dosing under strong light is what pushes the color toward rust and wine red.
  • Separate the culture into small clusters. Rinse the gel away and plant two or three plantlets per spot, spaced about an inch apart. Planting the whole mat as one lump kills the center.
  • Trim the tops, replant them, discard the base. Like most Ludwigia, older lower stems go leggy. Cutting the top few inches and replanting them keeps the group dense and evenly colored. Also available as fresh-cut stems.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Ludwigia Care Guide.

Notes

  • Appearance may vary depending on growing conditions. Plants may arrive in emersed form and will transition to submerged growth once planted in your aquarium. Some initial leaf melt may occur during acclimation.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Aponogeton Boivinianus
products.body_html:
Heavily textured leaves with real presence. Aponogeton boivinianus is a Madagascar bulb plant producing long, deeply crinkled, dark green leaves — the most strongly textured foliage in the genus. It makes an immediate centerpiece in a larger tank.

What You'll Receive

Healthy Aponogeton Boivinianus cultivated by Aquarium Plants Factory®, available in two variants:

  • Bulb Only: A firm, healthy bulb ready to sprout
  • Sprouted Bulb with Leaf: A healthy bulb with approximately 3–4 new sprouting leaves, already showing active growth

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Boivin's Aponogeton
  • Scientific name — Aponogeton boivinianus
  • Family — Aponogetonaceae
  • Origin — Madagascar
  • Plant type — Bulb / tuber
  • Foliage — Long, heavily crinkled, deep green
  • Placement — Midground to background; centerpiece in larger aquascapes
  • Growth rate — Medium to fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high
  • CO₂ — Not required; recommended for stronger growth
  • Water — 72–82°F; soft to moderately hard
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Propagation — Bulb division

Grower's Notes

  • The texture is the reason to buy it. Boivinianus carries the heaviest crinkling in the genus, and it holds that texture at size — where many textured plants smooth out as the leaves mature. Site it where side lighting rakes across the leaf.
  • Set the bulb on the substrate, don't bury it. Leave the top third exposed; buried bulbs rot.
  • A dormant rest is normal. The plant dies back and returns. Leave the bulb in place.
  • Minor leaf melt during acclimation is expected as it converts to your water. New growth follows.
  • Root tabs matter. A large fast-growing bulb plant runs through its reserves quickly and then stalls in inert gravel.

Notes

  • Growth rate, leaf size, and overall appearance may vary depending on aquarium conditions. Minor leaf melt can occur during acclimation.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Bucephalandra Red Catherine
products.body_html:
Red Catherine is one of the darker Bucephalandra varieties we grow — narrow, elongated leaves that hold a red-to-bronze tone rather than the blue-green of the common Buce types. It stays small, grows slowly, and needs no substrate at all.

What You'll Receive

Sold as loose Bare-Root or Potted plants:

  • 1 Bare-Root: Approximately 6+ leaves
  • 5 Bare-Root: Approximately 30+ leaves total
  • 10 Bare-Root: Approximately 60+ leaves total
  • 1 Potted: Approximately 10+ leaves
  • 5 Potted: Approximately 50+ leaves total
  • 10 Potted: Approximately 100+ leaves total

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Red Catherine Buce
  • Scientific name — Bucephalandra sp. 'Red Catherine'
  • Also known as — Buce Red Catherine
  • Origin — Borneo (genus range)
  • Placement — Midground, attached to hardscape
  • Mature height — 3-5 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Stronger light deepens the red and bronze tones; it will still grow under low light, just greener.
  • CO₂ — Not required. Improves growth rate and color if you already run it.
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — None needed. Epiphyte; feeds from the water column.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rhizome creeper; grows submersed or emersed
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower's Notes

  • Never bury the rhizome. Tie the horizontal rhizome to wood or rock and leave it exposed. Buried rhizomes rot.
  • Farm-raised, not wild-collected. All the Bucephalandra we carry is farm-grown, and much of it is raised from tissue culture rather than collected from Borneo.
  • Some leaf melt after shipping is normal. The rhizome survives it and pushes new submersed leaves within a few weeks — don't throw the plant away.
  • Red Catherine's color sits in the leaf itself rather than in a surface sheen, so it reads red across a wider range of viewing angles than the iridescent varieties.
  • Growth is slow enough that it rarely needs trimming. Plan the placement once and leave it.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Bucephalandra Care Guide.

Notes

Like most Bucephalandra, minor leaf melt may occur after introduction as the plant adjusts to new water parameters. This is normal and temporary — new submersed leaves regrow from the rhizome once the plant stabilizes.

Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Aponogeton Madagascariensis (Madagascar Lace)
products.body_html:
Leaves with the tissue missing. Aponogeton madagascariensis grows foliage that is pure lattice — a skeleton of veins with open holes where leaf blade would normally be. No other aquarium plant looks remotely like it. It is also genuinely demanding: cool, clean, moving water, and patience.

What You'll Receive

  • Sold as Bare-root Plants, Sprouts Bulb With Leaf, or Bulb Without Leaf:
  • Bare-root Plants: A healthy loose specimen without bulb
  • Sprouted Bulb with Leaf: A healthy bulb with at least two lace leaf already growing
  • Bulb Only (No Leaf): A firm, viable bulb without current foliage (ideal for patient aquarists)

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Madagascar Lace Plant
  • Scientific name — Aponogeton madagascariensis
  • Origin — Slow rivers and lakes of Madagascar
  • Plant type — Bulb / tuber
  • Placement — Background or centerpiece
  • Mature height — 10–16 in
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced
  • Light — Medium to high, but indirect. Harsh light burns the open leaf structure
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 68–75°F · pH 6.0–7.0. The temperature ceiling is the strictest of any plant we sell
  • Flow — Gentle to moderate, well oxygenated. Stagnant water rots the bulb
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — True aquatic. Does not grow emersed
  • Propagation — Bulb offsets

Grower’s Notes

  • Temperature is what kills it. Above about 75°F the lace plant declines regardless of everything else. In a standard tropical community tank at 78–82°F it will not survive long — this plant needs a cool, well-oxygenated tank of its own terms.
  • Clean water matters more than fertilizer. The open leaf structure traps detritus and grows algae easily; steady flow and regular water changes keep it clear.
  • Expect a dormancy. Lace plants often drop all their leaves and rest for weeks or months. Leave the bulb in place — it usually restarts.
  • Press the bulb only partly into the substrate; fully buried bulbs rot.
  • Buy the sprouted bulb if you want certainty. A bare bulb is cheaper but asks for patience with no guarantee.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Aponogeton Care Guide.

Notes

  • This is a sensitive and specialty plant not suited for beginners. Water quality, cool temperature, and stable parameters are key to long-term success. Bulbs may take time to adjust after shipping — please plant with care and patience.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

featured_image.alt: Aponogeton Madagascariensis (Madagascar Lace) aquarium plant, photo 3

products.title: Hydrocotyle Tripartita
products.body_html:
Want a carpet with recognizable leaves? Hydrocotyle tripartita creeps across the substrate on fine stems carrying bright green clover-shaped leaves — far more distinct at a glance than the grass and moss textures most carpets offer. It also climbs, which is where it gets interesting.

What You’ll Receive

Choose the format that suits your aquascaping needs:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Loose, freshly cut portion without root, ready to be planted or attached
  • Bunched Plants: Fresh-cut stems without root bundled with foam and plant weight for easy anchoring
  • Potted Plants: Fresh-cut stems without root potted in rockwool and net pot for stable placement and easy handling

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Hydrocotyle Japan
  • Scientific name — Hydrocotyle tripartita
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Mature height — 2–4 in
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium to high. Strong light keeps it flat; weak light makes it climb
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Root and water column feeder
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Creeping runners

Grower’s Notes

  • Light decides whether it carpets or climbs. Under strong light reaching the substrate it stays flat and spreads sideways. Under weaker light it grows upward, scrambling over rock and wood — which some aquascapers do on purpose for a vine effect.
  • Trim it often. It grows fast and will smother slower neighbors within weeks if left — this is a plant that needs managing, not a set-and-forget carpet.
  • Replant the trimmings. Every cut piece roots readily, so one portion covers a foreground quickly at no extra cost.
  • It attaches loosely to hardscape as it creeps, so you can wrap it around stone and let it hold on by itself.

Looking for the smaller version? Read our comparison of Hydrocotyle Tripartita vs Tripartita Mini.

Notes

  • As live plants, appearance may vary slightly. Fresh-cut and bunched plants may not have established roots but will develop quickly under stable aquarium conditions.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Amazon Sword (Small Size)
products.body_html:
The same Amazon Sword, bought small. Echinodorus bleheri ships here at 4-6 inches — a cheaper way into a plant that will still reach a foot and a half, and a size that suits a newly planted tank where a full specimen would look out of scale from day one.

What You'll Receive

Fresh, healthy Amazon Sword (Small Size) (Echinodorus bleheri) cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®.

Available in multiple growth forms:

  • Bare-root Plant — one healthy bare-root plant approximately 4–6 inches tall
  • Rooted Bunched — one rooted bunch containing approximately 1–2 healthy plants, secured with aquarium-safe foam and a plant weight
  • Rooted Potted — one healthy rooted plant grown in a nursery pot for easy planting

Simply plant the roots into a nutrient-rich substrate while keeping the crown (where the leaves emerge) above the substrate surface.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Amazon Sword, also known as Broad Leaf Amazon Sword
  • Scientific name — Echinodorus bleheri
  • Also known as — Echinodorus grisebachii 'Bleherae'
  • Origin — South America
  • Placement — Midground while young, background or centerpiece once grown
  • Shipped size — 4-6 inches
  • Mature height — 12-20 inches
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner, provided you feed the roots
  • Light — Medium. It reaches full size without high-output lighting.
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required. Steady growth either way.
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.5-7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Heavy root feeder — root tabs are not optional in inert gravel.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rosette; also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Adventitious plantlets on aerial floral stalks

Grower's Notes

  • Small is the shipping size, not the plant. This will not stay 4-6 inches. Under normal aquarium conditions it becomes the same 12-20 inch rosette as the full-size listing — so plant it where a large plant can live, not where a small one fits.
  • Feed it at the roots from the start. A young sword in inert gravel yellows, thins and develops holes in the older leaves. Root tabs or aquasoil under the crown are what turn a small plant into a large one.
  • Give it three inches of substrate depth. Set the crown at the surface, never below. The root mass gets substantial and a shallow bed stunts it permanently.
  • It propagates by floral stalk, not runner. Once settled it throws a tall stalk carrying plantlets. Leave each attached until it has four or five leaves and its own roots, then cut it free and plant it.
  • Expect a transition. Grown emersed, so some arriving leaves may die back as it converts to submerged growth. New leaves follow from the crown.

Other ways to buy this plant. Standard grade is the Amazon Sword; there is also a mother plant at 16-24 inches and a bulk pack.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Amazon Sword Care Guide.

Notes

Pictures are representative samples only. Live aquatic plants are natural products and may vary in size, color, and fullness depending on season and growing conditions. Plants are shipped approximately 4–6 inches tall and will continue to grow significantly larger under proper aquarium conditions. Amazon Sword is commonly grown emersed and may experience a normal transition period as it adapts to submerged aquarium conditions.

Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

featured_image.alt: Amazon Sword (Small Size) aquarium plant, photo 2

products.title: Bucephalandra Petite Blue Chili Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Petite Blue Chili is a nano Bucephalandra with an unusually wide color range — blue, violet, green and metallic tones that develop once the plant converts to submersed growth and shift with the tank it is in. At one to three inches it works as detail rather than mass.

What You'll Receive

  • One sealed 4-inch Vitro Culture® tissue culture bag
  • Approximately 4 small plantlets grown in sterile nutrient gel
  • 100% free from snails, algae, pesticides and pathogens
  • Rinse the gel away and separate the plantlets before planting

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Petite Blue Chili Buce
  • Scientific name — Bucephalandra sp. 'Petite Blue Chili'
  • Also known as — Buce Blue Chili
  • Origin — Borneo (genus range)
  • Placement — Foreground, attached to hardscape
  • Mature height — 1-3 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Leaves this small have no margin for algae, so keep it down.
  • CO₂ — Not required. Deepens color and speeds growth if you already run it.
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — None needed. Epiphyte; attaches to rock or driftwood.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rhizome creeper; grows submersed or emersed. Can flower year-round.
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower's Notes

  • Gentle flow suits it, mirroring the river it comes from. Bucephalandra are rheophytes — they grow on rock in moving water. Current keeps debris off the leaves, but too much lifts a small rhizome off its mount before the roots grip.
  • Rinse the gel off completely and separate the four plantlets before attaching. Leftover nutrient agar clouds water and feeds algae.
  • Never bury the rhizome. Tie it to wood or rock and leave it exposed; buried rhizomes rot.
  • Farm-raised, not wild-collected. All the Bucephalandra we carry is farm-grown, and much of it is raised from tissue culture rather than collected from Borneo.
  • Color is a property of your tank as much as the plant. Blue and violet develop over weeks under the right spectrum; under warm white the same plant reads plain green.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Bucephalandra Care Guide.

Notes

Disclaimer: Pictures are not the actual plants you will receive, but a sample representation. Unless specific, we don't guarantee aquatic plants will be free of pests, and pesticides, grow emerged, or submerge.

Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Micro Sword Narrow Leaf
products.body_html:
Micro Sword Narrow Leaf is the finest-bladed of the Lilaeopsis carpets. Where the standard micro sword reads as short grass, this one reads as fine turf — thin, upright blades that spread by runner into a low meadow with a much more delicate scale.

What You'll Receive

Choose the format that best suits your planting style:

  • Bare-root Plants — Small loose clusters, ideal for direct planting and precise spacing across the foreground.
  • Rooted Bunched Plants — Healthy rooted stems tied with weight for fast anchoring and easy placement.
  • Rooted Potted Plants — Fully rooted plants grown in rockwool, the easiest to plant and fastest to establish.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Narrow Leaf Micro Sword
  • Scientific name — Lilaeopsis mauritiana
  • Also known as — Micro Sword Narrow Leaf, Mauritius Micro Sword
  • Origin — Mauritius
  • Placement — Foreground
  • Mature height — 1-3 inches
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Nutrient-rich soil or root tabs; this is a root feeder
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rosette
  • Propagation — Runners

Grower's Notes

  • Split it into small plugs and space them out. Separate the portion into clusters of a few blades with roots attached and plant them an inch apart. Lilaeopsis fills the gaps by runner far faster than one clump grows outward.
  • It is slow to start and then steady. Expect very little visible progress for the first three or four weeks while the roots establish, then runners in every direction. Do not disturb it during the quiet phase.
  • Feed the roots. This carpet takes almost everything from the substrate. On inert sand without root tabs it survives but barely spreads; over aquasoil it closes properly.
  • Light reaches the base or the base dies. Once the carpet thickens, trim it back. Shaded lower blades brown off, lose grip and the mat lifts in patches.
  • Finer than standard micro sword. If you have used Lilaeopsis brasiliensis and found it coarse for a nano tank, this is the version to use — same habit, noticeably thinner blades.

Notes

  • Photos are for reference only. Actual plant size and density may vary. Some initial transition melting may occur as the plant adapts to submerged growth.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

featured_image.alt: Micro Sword Narrow Leaf aquarium plant, photo 2

products.title: Fissidens Nobilis
products.body_html:
Feathers, not fuzz. Fissidens nobilis grows flat, distinctly feather-shaped fronds in a single plane — and at a noticeably larger scale than Phoenix Moss, so the individual fronds are visible rather than merging into a mass. The most structured-looking moss we carry.

What You’ll Receive

  • Sold as a small loose portion
  • Approx. 2" x 2" in size
  • Perfect to attached to driftwood, rock, or stone

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Noble Fissidens
  • Scientific name — Fissidens nobilis
  • Placement — Foreground, attached to driftwood, stone or décor
  • Mature height — 1–2 in
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required, though it thickens growth
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Not required. Attaches to hardscape
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Fragmentation — divide and re-attach

Grower’s Notes

  • Frond size is what you're paying for. Most mosses read as texture from a distance. Nobilis is large enough that the feather shape stays legible — use it where it will be seen up close, not as background filler.
  • Tie it thinly and flat. The fronds grow in one plane, so pressing it flat against wood or stone gives the best result; a thick pad hides the structure and rots underneath.
  • Slow growth means it holds its shape for months without trimming — but also that algae, once in it, is very hard to clear.
  • Keep light moderate and flow steady; stagnant corners let detritus settle between the fronds.
  • Divide with scissors and re-attach the pieces — each fragment establishes independently.

Want to go deeper? Read our guide to aquarium moss varieties and how to attach them.

Notes

  • Pictures are not the actual plants you will receive, but a sample representation. Unless specific, we don't guarantee aquatic plants will be free of pests, pesticides, grow emerged, or submerge.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

featured_image.alt: Fissidens Nobilis Loose Portion Rare Aquarium Plants Factory® Moss

products.title: Echinodorus Martii
products.body_html:
A sword with texture instead of just size. Echinodorus martii grows broad, arching leaves with deeply ruffled edges that catch light along every wave — where a standard Amazon Sword gives you a smooth green fountain, this gives you a crinkled one. It grows large, so it wants a tank with room.

What You'll Receive

Sold as loose bare-root plants, bunched plants, or potted plants:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Approximately 1–2 individual bare-root plants
  • Bunched Plants: Approximately 1–2 plants bundled with foam and a plant weight
  • Potted Plants: Approximately 1–2 plants rooted in rockwool and net pot

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Martii Sword
  • Scientific name — Echinodorus martii
  • Also known as — Echinodorus major, Ruffled Amazon Sword
  • Origin — South America
  • Placement — Midground to background; centerpiece in larger tanks
  • Mature height — 10–16 in
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium
  • CO₂ — Not required, though it drives larger leaves
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.5–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Heavy root feeder — nutrient substrate and root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Adventitious plantlets on flower stalks

Grower's Notes

  • Give it space before you buy it. Mature leaves arch wide as well as tall, so one plant occupies a lot of a 20-gallon tank. In a nano it will simply outgrow the glass.
  • Feed at the roots. Swords take most of their nutrition from the substrate — root tabs under the crown do more than any liquid dosing.
  • Plant the crown at substrate level. Burying it rots the plant.
  • Expect the first leaves to melt as it converts from emersed nursery growth. The second flush is the ruffled submerged form.
  • It propagates from flower stalks, not runners. A mature plant sends up an inflorescence carrying plantlets along its length; let each root, then cut it free and plant it separately.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Amazon Sword (Echinodorus) Care Guide.

Notes

  • This plant grows large and is best suited for medium to large aquariums. Older leaves may melt back during transition; new growth will adapt to aquarium conditions.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Cryptocoryne Lucens
products.body_html:
Want a Crypt small enough for the foreground? Cryptocoryne lucens stays around 2–4 inches with slim, grass-like leaves — far narrower than the wendtii types most people start with — and spreads by runners into a low, dense group. It does that in low light, without CO₂. These are young plants grown in a controlled laboratory environment, so they arrive clean.

What You’ll Receive

  • Small Bare-root: 1 loose, small bare-root plant with 6+ leaves
  • Potted Plant: 1 plant with 6+ leaves, planted in rockwool inside a net pot
  • Young plants grown in a controlled laboratory environment (ex-vitro), offering a clean, pest-free start

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Crypt Lucens
  • Scientific name — Cryptocoryne lucens
  • Also known as — Cryptocoryne × willisii 'Lucens'
  • Origin — Sri Lanka
  • Placement — Foreground
  • Shipped size — Small plant, 6+ leaves
  • Mature height — 2–4 in
  • Suits — 5 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.5–7.5. Hard water suits it, as it does most Crypts
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Substrate runners

Grower’s Notes

  • Why two scientific names? Cryptocoryne lucens is treated by many botanists as part of the Cryptocoryne × willisii complex, so both names appear on the same plant. Nothing about the care changes.
  • This is the low-tech alternative to a carpet. It won't form a lawn like hairgrass, but it fills a foreground reliably where carpets fail.
  • Expect melt after planting. Crypts drop leaves on a change of conditions and rebuild from the roots over two to four weeks. Don't pull them.
  • Place it once. Every move triggers another melt.
  • Also available as sterile Cryptocoryne Lucens Vitro Culture if you want multiple plantlets in one bag.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Cryptocoryne Care Guide.

Notes

  • Cryptocoryne species may experience temporary "crypt melt" when introduced to new environments. This is normal and the plant will regenerate with proper care and stable conditions.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Hydrocotyle Tripartita Mini Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Half the leaf, half the height — and sterile. Hydrocotyle tripartita 'Mini' is a dwarf form of the standard clover pennywort: the same fast creeping runners and three-lobed leaves, but small enough to stay flat at 1–2 inches instead of climbing. This is the Vitro Culture® (tissue culture) format, so it arrives free of snails, algae and pesticide residue.

What You'll Receive

One 4-inch Vitro Culture® bag of Hydrocotyle Tripartita Mini, carefully grown in sterile conditions and ready to rinse, separate, and plant directly into your aquarium substrate.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Mini Hydrocotyle, Mini Pennywort
  • Scientific name — Hydrocotyle tripartita 'Mini'
  • Also known as — Hydrocotyle sp. 'Japan' Mini, Mini Clover Plant
  • Origin — Southeast Asia
  • Placement — Foreground
  • Shipped size — 4-inch Vitro Culture® bag
  • Mature height — 1–2 in
  • Suits — 5 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium to high. Light is what keeps it flat rather than climbing
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Runners — cut and replant sections

Grower's Notes

  • Light decides carpet or climber. Under weak light the runners stretch upward and it stops being a carpet. That is a lighting problem, not a plant problem — and it is the single thing that determines whether this works for you.
  • Rinse the gel off completely and separate into small portions before planting. Runners only travel into open substrate, so spacing decides how fast it closes.
  • Pin fresh portions down with weights or tweezers until roots grab; loose sections float free.
  • It grows fast. Trim runners every few weeks or it crosses into neighboring plants.

products.title: Water Hyacinth

Ideal for aquariums, Schismatoglottis Prietoi is known for its ease of care and adaptability to various water conditions. It prefers medium to low lighting and can flourish in temperatures ranging from 20 to 28°C. The plant's pH tolerance spans from 6.5 to 7.5, accommodating both soft and hard water types. While CO2 injection can promote faster growth, it's not a necessity for this plant.

Schismatoglottis Prietoi is particularly suited for smaller aquarium setups like Nano Cubes due to its compact growth pattern. It can be planted directly into the substrate or attached to hardscape materials like rocks and driftwood. This versatility, combined with its unique appearance and easy propagation through rhizomes, makes Schismatoglottis Prietoi a valuable plant for both beginner and experienced aquarists.

This species is a testament to the diversity and beauty of aquatic plants, offering a distinct look compared to more common aquarium plants like Anubias. It's a perfect choice for aquarists looking to create a natural, riverbed-like environment in their tanks.

  • You choose carpet or bush. Trimmed low and often it stays flat and spreads into a dense mat; left alone it branches upward into a bushy midground clump. Same plant, two different roles — decide before you plant rather than after.
  • It tolerates hard, alkaline water. Most stem plants want soft acidic conditions; this one runs to pH 8.0 without complaint, which makes it a genuine option for hard tap water where the usual midground choices sulk.

products.title: Java Fern Black Forest
products.body_html:
Dark, almost black-green leaves with a heavily textured surface, growing dense rather than open. Leptochilus pteropus 'Black Forest' is the Java Fern to reach for when a scape needs shadow and mass at the back — and it asks for nothing more than the plain green form does.

  • Bunched Plants: Approximately 6+ leaf portion bundled with foam and plant weight

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Black Forest Java Fern
  • Scientific name — Leptochilus pteropus 'Black Forest' (syn. Microsorum pteropus)
  • Origin — Cultivated form; the species ranges across Java, Malaysia, Thailand, northeast India and southern China
  • Placement — Midground to background, attached to driftwood, stone or décor
  • Mature height — 8-12 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5, soft to moderately hard
  • Substrate — Not required. Epiphyte — attach the rhizome to hardscape and never bury it.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious; grows emersed as well as submersed
  • Propagation — Rhizome division, plus plantlets from mature leaves

Grower's Notes

  • Dark plants need light behind them. Against black substrate and dark wood this variety vanishes. Set it where pale sand, light stone or bright green foliage sits behind or beside it and the depth of color becomes the point.
  • It grows dense, so it needs space. Unlike the open, upright plain form, Black Forest fills in. Give it more room on the hardscape than you think it needs, or the inner leaves shade themselves and thin out.
  • Never bury the rhizome. Roots may go into substrate; the thick horizontal stem must stay in open water or it rots — the usual way a Java Fern is lost.
  • Black spots on old leaves are baby plants, not disease. Leave a spotted leaf in place until each plantlet has roots and two or three leaves, then detach and attach it elsewhere. This is how one plant becomes a wall of them.
  • Expect a change of leaf. We grow this emersed, so some arriving fronds will die back as it converts to submerged growth. That is the plant working, not failing.

What You'll Receive

Fresh, healthy Java Fern (Leptochilus pteropus) cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®.

Bare-root Portion: Approximately 6 individual leaves with some roots attached. Leaves may arrive separated, and rhizomes are not guaranteed to be connected. This is completely normal for Java Fern and makes it easier to attach each plant to driftwood, rocks, or other hardscape.

Unlike some sellers, we do not tie multiple rhizomes together with black cotton thread to make them appear as one clump, as this can restrict healthy growth, and increase the risk of rot over time.

  • 5 Pack: 5 individual bare-root portions (approximately 6 leaves per portion)
  • 10 Pack: 10 individual bare-root portions (approximately 6 leaves per portion)
  • 20 Pack: 20 individual bare-root portions (approximately 6 leaves per portion)

For best results, attach each leaf or rhizome section to driftwood, rocks, or other hardscape using cotton thread. New rhizomes and plantlets will naturally develop as the plant grows.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Java Fern
  • Scientific name — Leptochilus pteropus (syn. Microsorum pteropus)
  • Origin — Southeast Asia
  • Placement — Midground, attached to driftwood, rock or décor
  • Mature height — 6-10 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required; it encourages faster growth and larger leaves but is not needed
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Not required. Epiphyte — attach the rhizome to hardscape and never bury it.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious; grows emersed as well as submersed
  • Propagation — Rhizome division, plus plantlets from mature leaves

Grower's Notes

  • Buy coverage, do not wait for it. Java Fern adds only a few leaves a year. Twenty portions spread across a large piece of wood look established the day they go in; one portion never will.
  • Separated leaves are a feature, not damage. Each leaf with a scrap of rhizome and a root will grow into its own plant, and separate pieces are far easier to distribute across a hardscape than one bound clump. That is why we do not thread them together.
  • Never bury the rhizome. Roots may go into substrate; the green horizontal stem must stay in open water or it rots — the single most common way a Java Fern is killed.
  • Black spots on old leaves are baby plants, not disease. Leave a spotted leaf in place until each plantlet has roots and two or three leaves, then detach and attach it elsewhere. A bulk planting becomes self-propagating within a year.
  • Expect a change of leaf. We grow this emersed, so some arriving leaves will die back as the plants convert to submerged growth. That is the plant working, not failing.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Java Fern Care Guide.

Notes

products.title: Amazon Sword | Bulk Pack
products.body_html:
One Amazon Sword fills a corner. Twenty fill a wall. Echinodorus bleheri is the standard background plant of the hobby — broad ribbed green blades, no CO₂ needed, and tough enough for cichlid and community tanks. This is the bulk pack, for furnishing a large aquarium or a shop in one go.

What You'll Receive

Fresh, healthy Amazon Sword (Echinodorus bleheri) cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®.

Each bundle is rooted and secured with aquarium-safe foam and a plant weight, containing approximately 1–2 healthy plants per bunch.

  • 5 Pack: 5 rooted bunched plants (approximately 1–2 plants per bunch)
  • 10 Pack: 10 rooted bunched plants (approximately 1–2 plants per bunch)
  • 20 Pack: 20 rooted bunched plants (approximately 1–2 plants per bunch)

Simply remove the foam and plant weight before planting if desired, and place the roots into a nutrient-rich substrate while keeping the crown above the substrate surface.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Amazon Sword, also known as Broad Leaf Amazon Sword
  • Scientific name — Echinodorus bleheri
  • Also known as — Echinodorus grisebachii 'Bleherae'
  • Origin — South America
  • Placement — Background
  • Mature height — 16-20 inches
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner, provided you feed the roots
  • Light — Medium. It reaches full size without high-output lighting.
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required. Steady growth either way.
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.5-7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Heavy root feeder — root tabs are not optional in inert gravel.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rosette; also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Adventitious plantlets on aerial floral stalks

Grower's Notes

  • Space them wider than you think. A mature Amazon Sword spreads a foot across. Twenty planted at four-inch spacing will shade each other out within a year — plant for the size they reach, not the size they arrive at, and use the spare plants elsewhere.
  • Bulk buying only pays if the substrate can feed them. Twenty heavy root feeders in inert gravel will all yellow together. Budget for root tabs across the whole planted area, or use aquasoil.
  • Give them depth. Three inches of substrate, crown set at the surface and never below. The root mass is substantial and a shallow bed stunts the whole planting.
  • Expect a transition. These are grown emersed, so some arriving leaves will die back as the plants convert to submerged growth. New leaves follow from the crown.
  • They propagate themselves. Settled plants throw tall floral stalks carrying plantlets. Leave each one attached until it has four or five leaves and its own roots, then cut it free — a bulk planting becomes self-replacing within a year.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Amazon Sword Care Guide.

Notes

Pictures are representative samples only. Live aquatic plants are natural products and may vary in size, color, and fullness depending on season and growing conditions. Amazon Sword is commonly grown emersed and may experience a normal transition period as it adapts to submerged aquarium conditions.

Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Red Tiger Lotus | Bulk Pack
products.body_html:
One hundred bulbs, priced for volume. Red Tiger Lotus (Nymphaea zenkeri) grows broad arrow-shaped leaves in deep red without CO₂ or high-output lighting — and at this quantity it becomes viable for pond planting, retail resale, or filling a large display. Bulbs are sold as-is: the sprout rate is high, but individual bulbs are not guaranteed.

What You'll Receive

  • 100 loose Red Tiger Lotus bulbs
  • May be dormant, semi-dormant, or already sprouting
  • Sold in bulk format, as-is, with no replacement or growth guarantee

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Red Tiger Lotus, Tiger Lotus
  • Scientific name — Nymphaea zenkeri 'Red'
  • Plant type — Bulb / tuber
  • Placement — Background or centerpiece; also suits ponds
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — High. Light intensity is what brings out the red and the mottling
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Heavy root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — True aquatic. This plant cannot be grown emersed
  • Propagation — Rhizome division; the bulb produces daughter bulbs

Grower's Notes

  • Plan for losses and it's still the cheaper route. At bulk pricing, even a proportion of duds costs less per grown plant than buying sprouted bulbs individually — which is the whole reason this pack exists.
  • Set each bulb on the substrate, don't bury it. Press it in far enough to stay put and leave the top exposed; buried bulbs rot rather than sprout.
  • Discard any bulb that is soft or shows rot before planting. One rotting bulb fouls the water around it.
  • Root tabs are not optional. In inert gravel these stay small and green instead of coloring up.
  • New growth usually appears within 10 to 15 days. Dormant bulbs may take longer — leave them in place before writing them off.
  • Need a guaranteed start instead? Single Red Tiger Lotus bulbs are available sprouted with leaf.

Notes

  • This is a bulk pack of Red Tiger Lotus bulbs. While most bulbs sprout reliably, some may not grow depending on tank conditions. Discard any that become soft or show signs of rot. Proper lighting and substrate will maximize your success.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Echinodorus parviflorus ‘Tropica’
products.body_html:
A sword that stays in proportion. Echinodorus parviflorus 'Tropica' grows dark green, distinctly ribbed leaves in a tight low rosette — the same fountain shape as an Amazon Sword at roughly half the footprint. It gives you a sword centerpiece in a tank that couldn't house one.

What You'll Receive

  • Sold as Bare-root Plants, Bunched plants, or Potted plants
  • Bare-root plants | 1 loose rooted plants
  • Bunched plants | 1-2 rooted plants bundle with foam, and lead weight
  • Potted plants | 1-2 rooted plants potted with net pot and rock wool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Tropica Sword
  • Scientific name — Echinodorus parviflorus 'Tropica'
  • Also known as — Echinodorus grisebachii 'Tropica', Rosette Sword, Dwarf Amazon Sword
  • Origin — South America
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Mature height — 8–14 in
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.5–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Adventitious plantlets on flower stalks

Grower's Notes

  • The compact size is the whole argument. A standard Amazon Sword overwhelms anything under 30 gallons. 'Tropica' holds the same silhouette without taking the tank over — which is why it works as a solitary specimen in a medium tank or a loose group in a large one.
  • Feed at the roots. Swords take most of their nutrition from the substrate; root tabs under the crown matter more than liquid dosing.
  • Plant the crown at substrate level, never below. Buried crowns rot.
  • Expect the first leaves to melt as it converts from emersed nursery growth — the second flush is the submerged form.
  • It propagates from flower stalks, not runners. A settled plant sends up an inflorescence carrying plantlets. Let each root and grow three or four leaves, then cut it free and plant it separately.

products.title: Bolbitis Heudelotii Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Fronds that catch the current. Bolbitis heudelotii — African Water Fern — grows deep green, almost translucent, feathered fronds that move constantly in flow. From fast rivers in tropical Africa, which is exactly why it looks best where water is actually moving. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® format.

What You'll Receive

Vitro Culture® (4-Inch Bag): One premium 4-inch sterile tissue culture bag containing approximately 1–2 healthy clumps of Bolbitis Heudelotii. Each culture is grown under sterile laboratory conditions and is 100% snail-free, algae-free, duckweed-free, and pest-free, making it ideal for aquascapers, shrimp tanks, and sensitive aquariums.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — African Water Fern
  • Scientific name — Bolbitis heudelotii
  • Origin — Tropical Africa
  • Placement — Midground to background, attached to driftwood, rock or décor
  • Mature height — 8–14 in
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required, though it drives fuller fronds
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5, soft to moderately hard
  • Substrate — Not required. Attaches to hardscape
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Usually grown submerged after acclimation
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower’s Notes

  • Flow is the difference between thriving and sulking. Bolbitis evolved in fast water and takes much of its nutrition from the passing current. Place it in a stagnant corner and it stalls; place it in the outflow and it thrives.
  • Never bury the rhizome. Tie or glue it to wood or rock — buried rhizomes rot.
  • Rinse all nutrient gel off before attaching, separate into portions, and expect a stall of several weeks while it converts to submerged growth. That pause is normal for the genus.
  • Slow growth plus translucent fronds means algae shows clearly. Keep light moderate and the tank balanced.
  • Divide the rhizome into sections with several fronds each once it has bulked up.

Notes

  • Pictures are for reference only and may not represent the exact plants you will receive. Tissue Culture plants are grown in sterile laboratory conditions and are 100% snail-free, algae-free, duckweed-free, and pest-free. Plant size, number of leaves, and clump size may vary naturally depending on the stage of growth at the time of harvest.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Giant Water Snowflake
products.body_html:
Round green pads floating on the surface with small white fringed flowers held just above them — Nymphoides indica gives a pond look inside an aquarium. Leaves can exceed four inches across, which makes this one of the larger plants in the Water Snowflake group.

What You'll Receive

Fresh, healthy Giant Water Snowflake (Nymphoides indica) plants cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®.

Available in convenient pack sizes:

  • Pack 1 Plant: Small fresh-cut plant with approximately 1 leaves (no roots or flowers).
  • Pack 5 Plants: Five small fresh-cut plants with approximately 1 leaves each (no roots or flowers).
  • Pack 10 Plants: Ten small fresh-cut plants with approximately 1 leaves each (no roots or flowers).

Plants are shipped as small fresh-cut plants. Once placed in the aquarium or pond, they will continue to grow and develop additional floating leaves under suitable conditions.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Giant Water Snowflake
  • Scientific name — Nymphoides indica
  • Also known as — Water Snowflake, Banana Plant relative; family Menyanthaceae
  • Origin — Tropical Asia, Africa and Australia
  • Placement — Floating, or rooted in substrate with leaves reaching the surface
  • Leaf size — Round pads over 4 inches across when mature
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium to high
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Optional; roots into soil or floats free
  • Growth habit — True aquatic with floating leaves
  • Propagation — Runners and plantlets at the leaf nodes

Grower's Notes

  • It arrives as a leaf, not a plant. Each pack is a small fresh-cut piece with about one leaf and no roots. Float it and it grows its own roots and further pads over the following weeks — the mature look in the photos takes a couple of months.
  • Let it float rather than planting it. Free-floating leaves get direct light and grow largest. Rooted in substrate it still works, but the pads stay smaller and take longer.
  • Plan for the shade it casts. Four-inch pads on the surface block a lot of light. That is useful over shy fish or to suppress algae, but anything light-hungry underneath will suffer.
  • Flowers need maturity and stability. The white fringed blooms appear on established plants in good conditions — not on a freshly shipped cutting.
  • It multiplies from the leaf nodes. New plantlets form where leaf meets stem; detach them once they have their own roots and you have free stock.

Notes

  • Appearance, size, and coloration may vary depending on growing conditions and season. Plants may arrive in their emersed (farm-grown) form and will transition to their submerged aquarium form after acclimation.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Bucephalandra Red Phantom Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Red Phantom comes from the Lamandau region of Borneo. Grown above water it shows green leaves on red stems — the stem color is the point of the variety. This is the tissue-culture format: sterile, snail-free, four plantlets per bag.

What You'll Receive

  • One sealed 4-inch Vitro Culture® tissue culture bag
  • Approximately 4 small plantlets grown in sterile nutrient gel
  • 100% free from snails, algae, pesticides and pathogens
  • Rinse the gel away and separate the plantlets before planting

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Red Phantom Buce
  • Scientific name — Bucephalandra sp. 'Red Phantom'
  • Also known as — Bucep Red Phantom, Buce Red Phantom
  • Origin — Lamandau, Borneo
  • Placement — Foreground to midground, attached to hardscape
  • Mature height — 2-4 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Too much light brings algae the plant is too slow to outgrow.
  • CO₂ — Not required. Improves color and pace if you already run it.
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — None needed. Epiphyte; attaches to rock or driftwood.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rhizome creeper; grows submersed or emersed
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower's Notes

  • The color is in the stem, not the leaf. Most Buce is bought for leaf tone; Red Phantom's appeal is the red petiole under a green leaf. That contrast only shows at close range, so place it at the front of the scape.
  • Rinse the gel off and separate the four plantlets before attaching. Leftover nutrient agar clouds water and feeds algae in the first weeks.
  • Never bury the rhizome. Tie it to wood or rock and leave it exposed; buried rhizomes rot.
  • Farm-raised, not wild-collected. All the Bucephalandra we carry is farm-grown, and much of it is raised from tissue culture rather than collected from Borneo.
  • Tissue-culture stock is emersed-grown and sheds some leaves as it converts to submersed growth. Give it several weeks before judging the color.

products.title: Nymphaea Golden West | Pink Tropical Water Lily
products.body_html:
A 1936 Randig hybrid still in the trade. Nymphaea 'Golden West' is a medium-sized tropical water lily bred by Martin E. Randig, producing cup to star-shaped blooms in a soft autumn-pink. New leaves emerge mottled with red before maturing to green, so the foliage shifts through the season alongside the flowers.

What You'll Receive

  • You will get 1 young and freshly harvested water lily tuber
  • All of our water lilies tubers/rhizomes have been inspected before ship out and guaranteed they are viable and perfect to grow in a proper pond environment

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Golden West Water Lily
  • Scientific name — Nymphaea 'Golden West'
  • Hybridizer — Martin E. Randig, 1936
  • Type — Tropical water lily
  • Flower — Autumn-pink, cup-shaped to star-shaped
  • Foliage — New growth mottled with red, maturing to green
  • Size — Medium
  • Placement — Ponds and container water gardens; also tanks 20 gallons and up

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Sunlight — Full sun; at least 6 hours of direct sun for good flowering
  • Water depth — 12 to 36 inches, in still or slow-moving water
  • Substrate — Heavy clay or loam in a submerged container
  • Planting angle — Tropical tuber: straight up at 90°, crown level with the soil
  • Feeding — Aquatic fertilizer tablets through the growing season
  • Overwintering — Tropical. Lift the plant in cold climates and store it warm and frost-free until spring
  • Propagation — Tuber division

Grower's Notes

  • Medium size is the useful part. Many tropicals want a large pond to look right. 'Golden West' stays moderate, which suits a smaller water garden where a full-size cultivar would cover the whole surface.
  • That moderate size also makes a tank realistic. Ponds take nearly all of these, but 'Golden West' will grow indoors in an aquarium of 20 gallons or more. Flowers are the hard part — they come only under very high, sun-like light run for long hours daily, so under standard tank lighting it behaves as a foliage plant. Keep cutting the pads back or they shade out everything below.
  • The red-mottled new growth gives two-tone foliage on an actively growing plant, before the pads settle to plain green.
  • A profuse bloomer, so the color keeps coming through the season rather than arriving in one flush.
  • Nearly ninety years in cultivation. Cultivars that stay in the trade that long do so on performance rather than novelty.
  • Tropical, so it cannot overwinter in a freezing pond. Lift the tuber before frost or treat it as an annual.

New to planting water lilies? Read our complete Water Lily Planting Guide — tuber angle, soil, depth and the one mistake that kills most first lilies.

Notes

  • We don't ship dormant roots. Your tuber arrives fresh and actively growing with 1–2 young leaves already emerged — visible proof it's viable before it leaves us. Young pads may start fully submerged and will reach the surface within about a week in good light.
  • Remove yellowing pads and spent flowers as they appear to keep the water clean and push energy into new growth.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Myriophyllum Elatinoides Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Myriophyllum elatinoides is a fast-growing stem plant with soft, feather-like leaves arranged in whorls around an upright stem. It is native to Central and South America, where it grows in cool streams and shallow margins. In an aquarium it forms a fine, flowing column that reads as movement rather than mass, which is why it earns its place in nature-style and Dutch layouts as a midground or background plant.

The foliage runs bright green under moderate light and picks up warmer, reddish tones as light intensity increases. Growth is quick enough that this is a plant you prune on a schedule rather than when you notice it — expect to top and replant every few weeks in a well-lit tank.

Growing Conditions

  • Light — Medium to high. Higher light drives the red tones and keeps internodes short.
  • CO₂ — Not required, but it makes the difference between an open, leggy stem and a dense one.
  • Substrate — Nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs.
  • Water — pH 6.0–7.5, 72–82°F (22–28°C).
  • Trimming — Frequent. Top the stems and replant the cuttings to build a thicker stand.
  • Placement — Midground to background.
  • Care Difficulty — Intermediate.

Grower's Notes

This is one of the faster stem plants we carry, and that cuts both ways. It will fill a background quickly, but it will also shade whatever is planted behind it if you let it run. Give it room at the back of the tank and stay ahead of it with the scissors.

Tissue culture stock arrives in its emersed form. The first set of submerged leaves will look finer and softer than what you unpack, and some of the original growth will melt off during the changeover. This is normal and not a sign of a problem — keep the light and nutrients steady and the plant will push new growth within a couple of weeks.

Vitro Culture® Advantages

  • Free from snails, algae, pathogens, and pesticides
  • Safe for shrimp tanks and other sensitive livestock
  • Keeps in the sealed bag under moderate light until you are ready to plant
  • Rinse the gel from the roots, separate into small portions, and plant with tweezers

What You'll Receive

One 4-inch sealed Vitro Culture® bag containing multiple Myriophyllum elatinoides plantlets, ready to be acclimated and planted in your aquarium.

Disclaimer

Photos are for reference only. Actual appearance and color may vary based on lighting and water conditions. Plant may melt slightly during transition from tissue culture to submerged life but will recover with proper care.

Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Alternanthera Ficoidea Rainbow
products.body_html:
Read this first: this is not a true aquatic plant. Alternanthera ficoidea 'Rainbow' is a garden and terrarium plant. Kept underwater it holds its red, yellow and green variegation for several months and then needs a spell of emersed growth to recover. Bought with that in mind, few plants carry this much color.

What You'll Receive

  • Sold as loose Fresh-cut Plants, Bunched plants, or Potted plants
  • Fresh-cut plants | approx. 5 stems, loose fresh-cut plants without root
  • Bunched plants | approx. 5 fresh-cut plants without root bundle with foam, and plant's weight
  • Potted plants | approx. 5 fresh-cut plants potted with net pot and rock wool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Rainbow Alternanthera
  • Scientific name — Alternanthera ficoidea 'Rainbow'
  • Also known as — Rainbow Joseph's Coat
  • True aquatic — No
  • Best suited to — Terrarium, vivarium, riparium, paludarium or bog planting
  • Origin — South America; widely cultivated as a garden plant
  • Placement — Midground
  • Shipped size — Approx. 5 fresh-cut stems, roughly 3-6 inches
  • Mature height — 4-8 inches
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up, or any humid terrarium
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high
  • CO₂ — Recommended when submerged
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich soil or root tabs; also feeds from the water column
  • Growth habit — Non-aquatic; submerged use is temporary, emersed growth is permanent
  • Propagation — Cuttings

Grower's Notes

  • This is not a true aquatic plant, and we would rather say so. Submerged it survives and even puts on a few inches over several months, but it does not grow indefinitely underwater. Plan to rotate it out to a humid emersed setup to recover, or treat it as a seasonal accent.
  • It is at its best above the waterline. In a riparium, paludarium, vivarium or bog planting with consistently wet soil and high humidity, the red-yellow-green variegation is far stronger and the plant grows without a time limit.
  • Light drives the color range. Under moderate light the foliage leans green. Strong light — bright LED or partial sun emersed — is what brings out the reds and yellows that give it the name.
  • Take cuttings before it declines. Root fresh tops in wet soil while the parent is still strong. Waiting until the submerged plant fades usually means the cuttings are too weak to take.
  • Want permanent color underwater? Alternanthera reineckii is the same genus, fully submersible, and stays red indefinitely.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Alternanthera Care Guide.
